title: "A bigger tally, one move at a time"
---

<!-- Made by the walk skill's render.py from the facts of the walk. Do not edit it by hand: run just walk-update again. -->

tally counts words, has tests, and writes a report. Now it grows as a real project does. It gets a dependency with
a range of versions, and a tool for its docs in a group of its own. It gets a page of docs with a picture, and a
library of its own in the same workspace. Then ruff passes its code. Last, it drops a dependency that it no longer
needs.

We make each change in moves. A move is one small change, made by one patch or by one command. You make each move,
and the page checks your files against it.

There are two ways to read this tutorial. Both have the same parts, in the same order.

Each part ends with a section called **What changed**. It lists every file that the part changes, with a link to the file, and then the whole diff of each file, folded. A lockfile and a binary file have a link alone. The text above it explains the change. In Build it yourself, What changed is what you check your files against.

In Build it yourself, a file that a command makes says which command. A diff that is open is a patch. Apply it with the command in the text, or make the same change in your editor.

## Build it yourself

Every command to run and every change to make by hand, to make the project yourself.

### Get the project

You build the project in a clone of your own, on a branch `mine` that starts where this walk starts. Run the commands of these pages in its top folder.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rahuldave/tally
cd tally
git switch -c mine 974d653080b0
```

Then add the command `git check`, which compares your files with the project's after each move, and leaves what `git add` has staged as it was.

```bash
git config alias.check '!f() { i="$(git rev-parse --git-path check-index)" && { cp -p "$(git rev-parse --git-path index)" "$i" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$i"; } && export GIT_INDEX_FILE="$i" && git add -A && git diff --cached --stat "$1"; }; f'
```
